checklist_items.label: The caller claims to be from Police, CBI, ED, Customs, Narcotics, TRAI, RBI, or a court.
checklist_items.explanation: Scammers rely on respected government and law-enforcement names (and often show fake uniforms or forged IDs) to override calm judgement.
checklist_items.action: Do not trust caller IDs, logos, or PDF notices sent on messaging apps. Verify independently through official local police or published agency portals.

checklist_items.label: They say your Aadhaar, PAN, SIM card, bank account, or a courier parcel is linked to a crime or money laundering.
checklist_items.explanation: False claims of illegal parcels, narcotics, or PMLA money-laundering cases are scripted to create sudden panic.
checklist_items.action: Real investigations do not begin with threats over an unsolicited call or demand instant compliance to prove innocence.

checklist_items.label: They mention 'digital arrest', an immediate arrest warrant, or police coming unless you cooperate right now.
checklist_items.explanation: There is no legal concept of 'digital arrest' in India. Law enforcement does not hold people under arrest via phone or video calls.
checklist_items.action: Hang up immediately. Real warrants and summons are served through lawful, verifiable offline procedures.

checklist_items.label: They insist you join or stay on a continuous video call (WhatsApp, Skype, etc.) and forbid disconnecting.
checklist_items.explanation: Keeping your camera on and refusing to let you hang up exhausts your critical thinking and isolates you from help.
checklist_items.action: End the call right away and turn off your camera—simply disconnecting breaks the scammer's control.

checklist_items.label: They tell you to stay alone, lock the door, or not tell family, friends, or bank staff.
checklist_items.explanation: Secrecy is demanded because anyone outside the call—a relative, friend, or bank teller—will quickly recognise the scam.
checklist_items.action: Immediately speak to a trusted family member, neighbour, or local police station.

checklist_items.label: They ask you to transfer money to a 'safe account', 'RBI verification account', or pay a 'refundable deposit/bail'.
checklist_items.explanation: No court, RBI office, or police agency ever asks citizens to transfer savings into another account to 'verify' funds or clear charges.
checklist_items.action: Never transfer any money, make a UPI payment, or share banking details for 'verification'.

checklist_items.label: They ask for OTPs, PINs, Aadhaar/PAN photos, or ask you to install a screen-sharing/remote-access app.
checklist_items.explanation: OTPs, PINs, and apps such as AnyDesk or TeamViewer give scammers direct access to drain accounts.
checklist_items.action: Do not share any codes or install apps on a caller's instruction.
